draft.title: Wave properties
card: Light is an electromagnetic wave. It is made of electric and magnetic fields that oscillate together and carry energy through space.
Electromagnetic waves are made by accelerating charges. A charge moving at steady speed does not make them, but a charge that speeds up, slows down or changes direction does.
Light is a transverse wave. The fields oscillate at right angles to the direction the wave travels.

All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum, c, about 3.00 × 10^8 m s^-1. This is true for radio waves, visible light and X-rays, whatever their frequency. The wave equation is c = fλ.
draft.remember: Accelerating charges make transverse electromagnetic waves, and in a vacuum all of them travel at c.

a.q: Which charge motion would produce an electromagnetic wave?
opts: An electron oscillating back and forth in an aerial
An electron moving at constant speed in a straight line
A proton at rest on a metal plate
A proton moving at constant velocity in a vacuum
a.why: An oscillating electron keeps changing its velocity, so it is accelerating and radiates an electromagnetic wave. A charge moving at steady speed in a straight line is not accelerating, so it does not. A fast charge is not enough: it must accelerate.
a.clue: Look for the charge whose velocity keeps changing.

b.q: A radio wave of frequency 100 MHz and a beam of red light both travel through a vacuum. How do their speeds compare?
opts: They are equal, and the radio wave has the longer wavelength
They are equal, and the radio wave has the shorter wavelength
The radio wave is faster because its wavelength is longer
The red light is faster because its frequency is higher
b.why: All electromagnetic waves travel at c in a vacuum, so the speeds are equal. Since c = fλ, a much lower frequency means a much longer wavelength, so the radio wave has the longer wavelength. Frequency does not change the speed in a vacuum.
b.clue: Speed is fixed in a vacuum, so use c = fλ to compare wavelengths.
